children: For a sustained move lower in the euro against the dollar, the currency pair needs another immediate catalyst, HSBC says in a currency outlook for 2027. That said, the euro is on the backfoot against the dollar as markets reprice the Federal Reserve outlook, its analysts say. French fiscal frailties remain in the spotlight, but less intensely than in October as OAT-Bund spreads have tightened, they add. "The growth-inflation mix has worsened in recent weeks, as eurozone activity surprises have trended lower while inflation surprises have moved higher," he says. The euro falls 0.3% to $1.0959, a 19-month low, according to LSEG. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
